overview: Freelook is a ghost-category camera module that decouples the rendered view from the server-visible rotation. While the bound key is held it steals the mouse deltas that vanilla would fold into rotationYaw and rotationPitch, accumulates them into its own lastYaw and lastPitch fields through the vanilla sensitivity gain curve, and forces third-person view. The player's actual rotation never changes, so the C03 look stream is frozen at the enable-time values and every attack-side rotation check sees a perfectly static stream. The comment in the source is explicit about the intent: looking around in vanilla third person changes the wire rotation and legit players get flagged by rotation checks while doing it, and this module exists to prevent that. The only packet interaction is receive-side: an S08 teleport with a forced look re-anchors the camera origin so the view does not snap back after the vanilla handler applies the new look.

sections.p: The split is the whole design. onEnable snapshots rotationYaw, rotationPitch and the third-person view mode; onRender2DEvent, which fires every render frame, reads mc.mouseHelper.deltaX and deltaY, scales them by f1 = (mouseSensitivity * 0.6 + 0.2)^3 * 1.5, the vanilla mouse-look gain curve, and adds them to lastYaw and lastPitch with the pitch clamped to +-90 degrees. None of that touches the player's rotation fields, so the server-side look, and every C03 look field derived from it, stays constant for as long as the module is held. handleInput() returns the enabled state so the fork's EntityRenderer can skip the normal mouse-look path and drive the third-person camera from the module's fields instead; the 5.99 snapshot has no net/minecraft tree to show that hook, but the contract is unambiguous. Because 1.8 getMouseOver ray-traces from the player rotation rather than the camera, Freelook grants no aim advantage: it is a pure awareness tool.

The single packet handler runs on the receive side. When an S08PacketPlayerPosLook arrives with a forced look, the vanilla handler writes its yaw and pitch into the player rotation and the client replies with a C06 ack. The module reads the same values and stores them as the new originalYaw and originalPitch, so the camera origin follows the forced look and the view does not snap back to a stale anchor after a teleport or set-back. The packet itself is neither cancelled nor modified, so the ack flow and the server-side teleport ledger behave exactly as vanilla.

The module is hold-to-activate: onRender2DEvent toggles itself off whenever the key is released or no key is bound, which is what makes the accumulation loop self-terminating. onDisable restores the original rotation and the previous third-person view mode, so the camera returns exactly to where it was. The Invert Pitch setting negates the snapshot pitch on enable, flipping the camera's vertical origin. The mouse-delta accumulation runs per render frame rather than per tick, so camera speed scales with framerate, a client-side artifact that never reaches the wire.

files.label: Freelook.java
files.explanation: The module file: the enable and disable snapshots, the per-frame mouse accumulation with the vanilla sensitivity curve and the +-90 pitch clamp, the hold-to-activate self-toggle, the handleInput() suppression contract for the fork's EntityRenderer, and the S08 receive handler that re-anchors the camera origin to a server-forced look. It also carries the Invert Pitch setting.

files.label: Module.java (event-handler base)
files.explanation: The base class defines the lifecycle every Rise 5.99 module uses: toggleModule() calls the overridden onEnable and onDisable, getKeyBind() supplies the key code the hold-to-activate check reads, and the default no-op handlers for onPacketReceive and onRender2DEvent show how Freelook's overrides slot into the event dispatch. The 204-line file is the wiring contract behind the module's handler set.

countering.label: fight Angle (rotation-window scoring)
countering.explanation: NCP's fight Angle chains AttackLocation entries over a 1000ms maxTimeDiff window and accumulates the yaw deltas between consecutive attacks. The frozen C03 look makes every delta zero, so angleVL never rises, and at the stock thresholds in this tree (move 100, time 150, yaw 60, switch 50) even active aim streams rarely trip the check. Freelook is therefore invisible to it twice over: the module was built precisely to keep the wire rotation static, and the check is dormant by default. The same frozen stream is what makes the module safe against every attack-side rotation check.

countering.label: AimbotHeuristic (click-gated mouse analysis)
countering.explanation: Hawk's AimbotHeuristic samples mouse-move vectors and only scores them around interactions: InteractEntityEvent or InteractWorldEvent arm the click window. Its three branches need real motion, a stutter requires maxSpeed minus minSpeed over 4 with minSpeed under 0.01, a twitch requires consecutive speeds over 20 degrees per move with an angle over 2.86 radians, and a jump requires a speed drop over 30 with a sharp angle. Freelook's zero-delta stream satisfies none of them, and a user who only looks around without attacking never arms the click window at all. It is an honest boundary, not a counter.

countering.label: KillAura (attack-side direction)
countering.explanation: Arc v2's KillAura Direction sub-check computes the angle between the entity vector and the player's look direction and punishes when it exceeds max-direction-angle, default 1.2 radians in config.yml, while the reach sub-check measures center distance minus victim velocity against max-reach 4.2. Because Freelook never changes the server-visible rotation, the attack geometry the server computes is exactly what vanilla aim produces; there is no off-axis component to score. The module is aim-neutral by construction, which is the honest reason no attack-side check can bite.

countering.label: TeleportQueue (S08 ack ledger)
countering.explanation: The S08 re-anchor is the module's only packet interaction, and it is read-only. TeleportQueue records each server teleport, matches the follow-up C06 by isSamePosAndLook, and ages unmatched entries out after 4000ms. Since Freelook neither cancels nor rewrites the S08, the ack matching sees an unmodified vanilla flow and the ledger never leaves the IDLE state on the module's account. This entry documents that the receive-side handler has no server-visible effect.
